abstract.para: The first step in the installation is booting the &agama; installer.

step.para: Copy the ISO image to the VIOS server:
Replace VIOS_SERVER with the hostname or IP address of your VIOS server.
Create a virtual optical device and load the ISO into the virtual device on the VIOS server:
Replace vcdXY with your virtual device unit attached to the LPAR you want to boot.

Boot the system from the attached virtual device. Select Select Boot Options Select Install/Boot Device CD/DVD List All Devices and select the virtual optical device you created in . Then select Normal Boot Mode and confirm your selection.
Log in to the console to get the &rootuser; password and IP address.
Select agama‐installer and press to boot the system.

step.para: Open a Web browser and point it to the given URL in the console. Enter the &rootuser; password and proceed with the installation.
Download &installer.iso; and mount it:
For installation in an air-gapped environment or without registration, download &full.iso; and mount it.
Use the following parmfile to start the installation:

example.title: Example parmfile
example.screen: cio_ignore=all,!condev,!0.0.0160 rd.zdev=dasd,0.0.0160 rd.zdev=qeth,0.0.0800:0.0.0801:0.0.0802,layer2=1,portno=0 ip=&wwwip;::192.168.3.254:24::enc800:none ip=192.168.3.100::192.168.3.254:24:SLE16-Beta2:enc800:none hostname=&wsI; nameserver=&dnsip; root=live:ftp://&ftpip;/agama/LiveOS/squashfs.img live.password=linux

callout.para: Only expose the devices that the machine should be aware of

IP configuration. The different parameters are separated by colons (:). You can omit unneeded parameters by leaving them out, meaning you get two or more subsequent colons. For a complete configuration reference, refer to man 7 dracut.cmdline.
If no IP configuration is specified, it will be assigned with DHCP and the IP address will displayed on the console after boot.

important.title: Multiple network interfaces
important.para: If your system has more than one network interface, IP configurations may be swapped after the installation, leaving the system unreachable.

To prevent this from happening, either bind each IP configuration to a particular interface by interface name or MAC address. If you use a MAC address, make sure to format it as 00-11-22-33-44-55 instead of 00:11:22:33:44:55

tip.para: As the console is hard to read on x3270, configuring the network in the parmfile is recommended.

callout.para: IP address of the gateway for the system
Host name of the system. You can also set the host name in the ip parameter, however it is transient whereas hostname gets written to /etc/hostname.
IP address of the DNS server for the system
URI of the installer ISO mounted in . For installation in an LPAR, use the ISO file directly as in:

Password for the system administrator &rootuser;. If you do not set a password, a random password will be generated and displayed on the console after boot. As the console is hard to read on x3270, setting a &rootuser; password in the parmfile is recommended.

step.para: Adjust your parmfile accordingly:
If you are using a VLAN, add the vlan parameter. Make sure to specify the virtual device instead of the underlying physical device.

tip.title: ifcfg vs ip syntax
tip.para: Earlier versions of &sle; used linuxrc with interface configuration (ifcfg) files, whereas &sle; 16 uses dracut with ip syntax for &nm;. While &agama; supports translating some options, it is recommended to use the new and more powerful syntax.
For a complete list of dracut options, refer to man 7 dracut.cmdline.

note.title: DASD alias devices
note.para: DASD alias devices are special in that they appear not operational until at least one associated DASD base device has been enabled. As a result, the &agama; installer cannot determine their actual type (ECKD or FBA DASD).

As a workaround, specify dasd-eckd as the device type. This should provide chzdev with enough information to create udev rules for enabling these devices even in the absence of a working device. When the base device is enabled later, and the alias devices become operational, they will be automatically set online.

step.para: Open a web browser pointing to the given IP address from the parmfile. Enter the &rootuser; password and proceed with the installation.
Select a bootable media and start the installation process.
For a bare-metal server, select the device or storage volume from which to boot.
For a virtual machine guest, select the path to the image file. Configure the virtual machine for the expected workload.
In the &grub; boot menu, select agama‐installer.
